newsitem.title: UK: UK 96/97 wheat crop seen closer to 16 mln T--HGCA. [CORRECTED 01:20 GMT 27/9/96]
newsitem.headline: UK 96/97 wheat crop seen closer to 16 mln T--HGCA. [CORRECTED 01:20 GMT 27/9/96]

text.p: Provisional June Scotland census and other more recent yield reports suggest the UK 1996/97 wheat crop could be closer to 16 million tonnes than 15 million, UK's Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said.
The HGCA, in a commentary published in its latest weekly bulletin, however kept barley crop estimates at between 7.5 million and 8.0 million tonnes.
In 1995/96, UK produced 14.31 million tonnes of wheat and 6.85 million of barley.
British agri-trade firm Allied Grain (Corrects from Dalgety Grain) on September 17 put the 1996/97 wheat crop at 15.74 million tonnes.
The HGCA said the provisional June Census for Scotland released last week all but completed the UK arable area data for this year's harvest.

"These figures point to a 5.6 percent rise in the UK wheat and barley area, and a 2.3 percent rise in oilseed rape sowings." it said. Wheat yields are estimated at 8.02 tonnes per hectare, up from last season's 7.70 tonnes.
The HGCA said early assessments of the wheat balance put this season's export availability at between 4.5 million and 5.0 million tonnes, versus exports of 3.1 million in 1995/96.
Initial barley export availability estimates generally range at between just under 2.0 million to 2.5 million tonnes, compared with 1.32 million a year ago.
"Hence, unless barley exports significantly improve, it seems likely than substantial intervention offers will be received this season," the HGCA said.
